## Choosing Postpaid AT&T or a Prepaid eSIM


The profile is only a container. The choice is which service that profile should carry.


### Keep the AT&T line you already pay for


If the number, the bill, and the account are already yours, stay on that postpaid line. The work is a number transfer, account verification, and a device eligibility check. Don't start a second plan because the first install looked slow. A second plan can split texts and data across two lines and leave you paying twice.


You'll often be asked for billing details or a ZIP code during that transfer. Answer for the account that owns the number. A family manager may need to approve the device change before the eSIM will download. Wi-Fi and a successful profile install are still required. Postpaid doesn't skip those steps.


A locked phone blocks both choices. If the iPhone was bought overseas or from another carrier and still shows a lock,[phone unlocking guidance for Perth residents](https://ctf.com.au/mobile-phone-unlock/) explains the kind of carrier release you need before any U.S. eSIM can stick.

## Fix a Failed AT&T iPhone eSIM Install


The camera beeped. The QR screen closed. The phone is still offline. Treat that as a provisioning and compatibility miss, not as a reason to scan the same square again.


### Check the account before the camera


Confirm four things in order.


- **The model supports eSIM.** An XS, XR, or later iPhone with no carrier lock is the floor. Older hardware won't grow the feature.
- **iOS is current.** An outdated system drops carrier prompts and transfer options.
- **Wi-Fi is stable.** Activation still needs the internet you started with. Cellular can't carry the download if cellular isn't up.
- **The line and the identity match.** The AT&T account needs the correct **IMEI** or **EID** and an eligible line. A wrong EID, or a QR code that was already used, blocks activation even when the camera reads the image perfectly.


Restart the iPhone once, rejoin Wi-Fi, and look again for the AT&T line under Cellular. If the scan itself failed, use **Enter Details Manually** rather than a third pass over a blurry code. If the scan succeeded and the line never appeared, the next move is a fresh code or a corrected EID from the carrier, not another photo of the old one.


There's no public AT&T success-rate figure worth chasing. Judge the install by whether a call and data work, not by how fast the QR screen disappeared.


### Prove the new line before you touch the old one


Turn the new AT&T line on under **Cellular** . Then run three tests, in this order, before you change anything else.


1. **Place an outgoing call** to a number you know will answer.
2. **Send an SMS** and confirm it arrives.
3. **Load a page on cellular data** with Wi-Fi switched off.


Set the intended default voice line and default data line in Settings so a second eSIM doesn't keep the phone on the old plan. Only after those three tests pass should you disable or remove the previous line.


Don't delete the existing eSIM until the new line can call, text, and use data. The profile is software. There's no plastic card to push back in. Recovery generally means the carrier reissues or reprovisions it.


If Wi-Fi won't hold or the phone has physical damage, another profile won't help.[iPhone repair shops in Pennsylvania](https://repairseeker.com/pa/iphone-repair/) are a reasonable stop when the handset itself can't stay online. Otherwise the decision list is short. Retry on solid Wi-Fi, correct the IMEI or EID on the account, use a fresh code or manual details, or contact the carrier for a new profile.


## Confirm the Line and Take the Next Step


Before you box the old phone, run the four milestones once, in order. Wi-Fi was connected. The AT&T profile is installed. The line is turned on. A call, a text, and a data session all succeeded with Wi-Fi off. Remove the old profile only after that sequence, not before.


Open **Settings > Cellular** one last time and check the default voice line and the default data line. A second eSIM can stay installed and keep calls or data on the plan you meant to retire. If both lines show on, the labels under Cellular tell you which one is in use.


What you do next depends on which milestone failed.


If the existing AT&T line now calls, texts, and loads data, you're done. Keep the QR image or the account details only if the carrier told you a reissue might be needed later. You don't need to scan anything again tonight.

It doesn't skip a locked phone.


If a fresh code and a correct EID still won't install, stop deleting profiles. Contact AT&T, or the prepaid provider, and ask for a reprovision. Another random delete leaves you with no line at all and a wait for a new software profile.


The phone is either verified by a live call and a data test, or you have one specific place to go next. Don't split the difference by wiping the only working eSIM "just to try."
